Who it's for

For the people who go outside,
and the people who plan it.

Astronauts

Know your own decompression risk before the hatch opens, and get prep tips that add safe hours outside.

Flight surgeons

A measured, per-person number instead of a population average to clear, hold or adapt an EVA.

Mission planners

See each crew member's risk on the calendar and move prep or EVAs before conflicts.

Agencies & stations

Artemis lunar EVAs and commercial stations flying more spacewalks with smaller medical teams.

Down on Earth, the same bubble physics: divers · high-altitude pilots · hyperbaric medicine
Business

Every safe hour outside is mission value.

Value

More work per spacewalk

  • Efficiency margin: low-risk crew can safely stay out longer
  • Safety margin: catch the high-risk day before the hatch opens
  • Shorter, smarter prebreathe frees crew time
Model

Licence + software per crew

  • Agencies: licence and integrate with mission-ops planning tools
  • Commercial stations: per-crew subscription, astronaut + planner apps
  • Earth: dive, aviation and hyperbaric spin-offs
Edge

A number that is personal

  • Decompression models are population models
  • One breath turns them into this crew member, today
  • Built on published NASA decompression data
